canonical_question: Is the 'as-cast alloy' referenced as the baseline (1010 MPa) the exact Nb20Mo20Cr20Ti20Al20 composition, or does it have a different stoichiometry?

question_variants.question: Is the 'as-cast alloy' referenced as the baseline (1010 MPa) the exact Nb20Mo20Cr20Ti20Al20 composition, or does it have a different stoichiometry?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The paper references an 'as-cast alloy' with a strength of 1010 MPa as a baseline for comparison, and while the specific stoichiometry of the cited work is mentioned in the evidence as NbMoCrTiAl, the text does not explicitly confirm the 'as-cast' baseline is the *exact* same composition without referencing the specific cited work's details fully, but implies it is the NbMoCrTiAl system.

answers.answer: The paper references an as-cast alloy with a compressive strength of 1010 MPa and low density (7.58 g/cm^3) which was designed by B. Gorr et al. with an equiatomic composition of NbMoCrTiAl. The text states the new composite's strength is 'increasing by more than a half than that of the as-cast alloy (1010 MPa)'.
answers.boundary_limitation: The text relies on a citation for the full details of the as-cast alloy, but confirms the composition is equiatomic NbMoCrTiAl.
evidence_spans: Therefore, on the basis of design principles above, a new RHEA with equiatomic composition of NbMoCrTiAl was designed by B. Gorr et al. [ [13] , [14] ].
The as-cast alloy with low density (7.58 g/cm 3 ) exhibits excellent oxidation resistance.
The declining oxidation rate at 1100 °C was mainly due to the formation of Al, Cr-rich oxide layers.
